description: THE RULE ITSELF, in the profile that claims none of these names (issue #841). Seven declarations of names belonging to four OPTIONAL profiles — Sprites, Interaction & Events, Geometry and Sound — are checked under `profiles: ["core-language"]` alone, and every one raises `ol-reserved-word`. `spec/grammar.md:382`: "The grammar has exactly four declaration slots ... A built-in name in any of those slots raises `ol-reserved-word`. Nothing shadows", and `:408` supplies the reason a profile cannot soften it — a program cannot declare which profiles it requires, so a name declarable under one profile set and not another would make conformance implementation-dependent, "invisible and unpredictable to a learner". This fixture lives under `core-language/` deliberately: after #841 the declaration rule is Core's rather than each profile's, so a Core-only program is the case that decides it. The per-profile OFF-halves (`sprites/reserved-procedures-without-sprites`, `interaction-events/block-heads-free-core-only`, `geometry/check/reserved-word-not-gated-without-geometry`, `heritage/check/heritage-alias-redefinition-legal-in-core`) each pin one profile's names and were inverted by #841 (three from clean to raising, and `heritage-alias-redefinition-legal-in-core` from nine diagnostics to thirteen); this one pins the rule they now share, so removing the rule reddens a Core fixture rather than only profile ones. The seven declarations cross the predicate's internal branches rather than sampling one of them: `ask` and `when` are profile KEYWORDS (Sprites and Interaction & Events, from `OL_PROFILE_KEYWORDS`); `grid`, `new_turtle`, `wait` and `set_tempo` are registered PRIMITIVES of Geometry, Sprites, Interaction & Events and Sound, which reach the predicate through a different lookup; and the seventh, `struct tell`, uses the `struct` declaration slot rather than `define` — `spec/grammar.md:165` makes them separate slots, so a fix reaching only `define` would leave that line clean. `"check": true`: these are checker diagnostics — nothing is called, no struct is instantiated, and no events are produced.
